purpose: Numerical arrays — hydrograph computation, signature statistics, matrix operations

np.nanpercentile.note: Use instead of np.percentile when the array may contain NaN (common in streamflow gaps).
np.nanpercentile.example: q05 = np.nanpercentile(q, 5)  # flow exceeded 95% of the time

np.log.note: log(0) = -inf; log(-x) = nan. Always guard with np.where(q > 0, np.log(q), np.nan) for streamflow.

gotchas: Integer overflow: np.array([1, 2, 3]) defaults to int64 on 64-bit. Mixing with float produces float — but np.zeros(n, dtype=int) + 0.1 silently truncates.
In-place operations on views: a = b[:5]; a += 1 modifies b. Use a = b[:5].copy() for independent array.
np.sum vs Python sum: np.sum(arr) is vectorised and handles NaN-less arrays; Python sum() is slow on numpy arrays.
Axis convention: axis=0 reduces along rows (over time), axis=1 reduces along columns. Easy to confuse for 2-D model output.
Boolean indexing: q[q > 0] returns a copy, not a view. Assigning to q[q > 0] = 0 modifies the original.
NaN propagation: np.mean with a NaN returns NaN. Use np.nanmean, np.nanstd, np.nanpercentile for streamflow arrays.
numpy 2.0 changed: np.string_ is removed — use np.bytes_; np.bool is removed — use np.bool_.
Floating-point equality: never use == for floats. Use np.isclose(a, b, rtol=1e-5) or np.allclose.

common_patterns.runoff_ratio:
mean_q = np.nanmean(q_mm)
mean_p = np.nanmean(p_mm)
runoff_ratio = mean_q / mean_p if mean_p > 0 else np.nan
common_patterns.fdc_slope:
q_sorted = np.sort(q)[::-1]
q10 = np.nanpercentile(q_sorted, 90)
q90 = np.nanpercentile(q_sorted, 10)
fdc_slope = (np.log10(q10 + 1e-9) - np.log10(q90 + 1e-9)) / (0.9 - 0.1)
common_patterns.nse:
def nse(obs, sim):
    mask = ~np.isnan(obs) & ~np.isnan(sim)
    num = np.sum((obs[mask] - sim[mask]) ** 2)
    den = np.sum((obs[mask] - np.mean(obs[mask])) ** 2)
    return 1 - num / den if den > 0 else np.nan
